pairs.subject: llm-price-book-operations
pairs.evidence: crates/store/src/sqlite/prices.rs:16 The stored rate card is a fixed input/output/cached-read trio with no cache-write class (let alone TTL-tiered writes), so premium cache-write traffic can only be priced as plain input or not at all — the under-pricing direction the standard names — and a past dated row can be overwritten in place through the upsert's ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.

techniques.evidence: crates/store/src/sqlite/prices.rs:16 Variants do live in the model key (the price_fill test keys a row "acme/zoo-1@batch"), but the rate card is the fixed trio the technique rejects. It has no cache-write rate and no TTL tiers, and config/pricing.json's non-coverage note does not declare that gap.

crates/store/src/sqlite/price_fill.rs:99 The backfill goes through the same PriceBook::cost_usd_mode resolver as ingest, so there is one resolution path. A miss leaves the row NULL (test an_unpriceable_key_fills_nothing_and_terminates).

crates/store/src/sqlite/price_fill.rs:95 Only NULL-cost rows can be written, so stamped costs are never restated. Filled rows are labelled cost_source=book_fill plus priced_at (pricing.rs FILL_SOURCE), and the test asserts a client-costed row stays at 99.0.

crates/store/src/sqlite/prices.rs:17 Every row stores effective_from, source_url, verified_at and note. list() hides future-dated rows and history() keeps the timeline. Measuring and showing book age happens in the api crate (measure_posture), outside this context.

crates/store/src/sqlite/prices.rs:27 Persist-then-reread is supported (upsert, then list() re-reads the DB for the rebuild). But the store accepts any caller-supplied effective_from and overwrites an existing dated row in place, despite the module doc calling the table append-only. The api put_price (crates/api/src/prices_fill.rs:108) passes the client's effective_from straight through, so an admin can backdate a rate or rewrite the one that priced last quarter.

pairs.registryProposal: no-retroactive-repricing says an imputed charge is 'never written onto the event'. This repo instead writes a labelled forward-fill (cost_source=book_fill, priced_at) onto previously NULL events, using the current book rather than the rate in force at event time. The technique should say whether a provenance-labelled one-time fill of unpriced rows is allowed, or whether it must stay a projection beside the ledger.
